![](data:image/png;base64,)Encapsulation of starch hydrogel and doping nanomagnetite onto metal-organic frameworks for eﬃcient removal of fluvastatin antibiotic from water

Asmaa K. Mohamed, Mohamed E. Mahmoud[\*](#_bookmark0)

_Faculty of Sciences, Chemistry Department, Alexandria University, Moharem Bey, Alexandria, Egypt_

A R T I C L E I N F O

_Keywords:_

Fluvastatin drug Starch hydrogel MOFs

Magnetite nanoparticles Factors optimization

Kinetics-isotherm-thermodynamics study

A B S T R A C T

Growing interests and efforts have been recently focused on design and assembly of novel hydrogel nanosorbents for removal of drugs from wastewater. Therefore, this work is aimed to immobilize and encapsulate starch hydrogel matrix onto metal organic frameworks (MOFs) and dope with nanomagnetite. The magnetic MOFs-Starch hydrogel (NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel) was synthesized via microwave irradiation process and characterized with high surface area (528.39 m2/g), mesoporous with pore size 2.90 nm and highly crystalline structure. The maximum swelling ratio (1000.0 %) was optimized at pH 10, 180 min and 25 °C. The validity of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel for adsorptive removal of Fluvastatin statin drug provided maximum equi-librium adsorption capacity 782.05 mg g−1. The Langmuir isotherm and pseudo-second kinetics models were correlated well with the computed correlation coeﬃcient values 0.9991 and 0.9997, respectively. The validity of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel for removal of FLV statin drug from real water matrices was confirmed in the

range 96.15–99.99 %.

1. Introduction

Fluvastatin (FLV) is a synthetic inhibitor for 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-glutaryl coenzyme A reductase, which is known to act as the rate lim-iting enzyme for cholesterol biosynthesis in the liver and is commonly used to improve lipid profiles in patients with primary hypercholes-terolemia and mixed dyslipidemia ([Dietrich, Webb, & Petry, 2002](#_bookmark28); [Dai](#_bookmark27) [et al., 2020](#_bookmark27); [Fabbri & Franzellitti, 2016](#_bookmark31); [Mathew & Rajagopal, 2017](#_bookmark48)). Due to their prevalent use, resistance to hydrolysis and confined human metabolism, statin drug excessively detected in surface water eﬄuents ([Janssens, Mandal, Dubey, & Luis, 2017](#_bookmark35); [Nassar, Ahmed, & Raya, 2019](#_bookmark51); [Sarker, Song, & Jhung, 2018](#_bookmark64)). Laboratory exposures to environmentally relevant concentrations have produced effects in fish and plants, re-sembling pathology observed in wild populations ([Kowalski et al.,](#_bookmark22) [2006](#_bookmark22)). Recent laboratory research has reported that small amounts of medication in drinking water can affect human embryonic kidney cells, human blood cells and human breast cancer cells ([Razavi, Song,](#_bookmark63) [Santoke, & Cooper, 2011](#_bookmark63); [Santos et al., 2016](#_bookmark67); [Tete, Nyoni, Mamba, &](#_bookmark72) [Msagati, 2019](#_bookmark72)).

Removal of these bio-accumulative pollutants from water is a cri-

tical issue to overcome the serious effect of these pollutants on water quality ([An, Liang, & Zhao, 2011](#_bookmark24); [Namazi, Heydari, & Pourfarzolla,](#_bookmark53) [2014](#_bookmark53); [Pandey, Do, Kim, & Kang, 2020](#_bookmark56); [Pandey, Do, Kim, & Kang, 2020](#_bookmark57)).

Hydrogel is three-dimensional networks constructed by physical or chemical crosslinking of polymer chains. The porous three-dimensional structure and polar functional groups endorse hydrogel outstanding performances on scavenging drugs ([Javanbakht, Pooresmaeil, &](#_bookmark20) [Namazi, 2019](#_bookmark20); [Pooresmaeil & Namazi, 2018](#_bookmark58)). Specifically, the porous structure renders hydrogel high specific surface areas, enabling large numbers of adsorption sites exposed to target drugs ([Fang et al., 2018](#_bookmark32)). The dense functional groups are capable of binding drugs ([Takei,](#_bookmark71) [Yoshihara, Danjo, Fukuhara, & Yoshida, 2020](#_bookmark71)). In addition, hydrogel can absorb water without losing its structural integrity, which facil-itates the separation and recycling of the hydrogel adsorbents from treated eﬄuents. Therefore, in the past decade, hydrogel has become a well-known and promising adsorbent for sequestrating drugs from polluted water ([Pooresmaeil & Namazi, 2020](#_bookmark59)). A three-dimensional graphene porous hydrogel was investigated with respect to the cipro-floxacin adsorption mechanism and moisture contents impact ([Yu, Sun,](#_bookmark77) [Yang, & Ma, 2019](#_bookmark77)). A study for enhanced adsorptive removal of some antibiotics from aqueous solutions was reported by the use of triple-network nanocomposite hydrogels from a combination of carbon na-notubes-graphene oxide-sodium alginate ([Ma, Jiang, Cao, & Yu, 2020](#_bookmark41)). Adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of sulfamethoxazole drug by a novel synthesized (p(HEA/NMMA)-CuS) hydrogel catalyst using ir-radiation polymerization and in-situ precipitation methods was

successfully studied ([Yang, Li, & Zhu, 2017](#_bookmark78)). On the other hand, Starch-hydrogels have various potential properties as biodegradability, bio-compatibility, low cost as well as non-toxicity. Starch is the most abundant polysaccharide stored in plants ([Namazi & Mosadegh, 2011](#_bookmark52)). It consists of distinct units of glucose molecules linked together with α-

D (1–4) and α-D (1–6) bonds. Starch-hydrogels have a variety of ap-

plications as drug delivery, food preservative, water treatment, tissue engineering as well as personal care products ([Ismail, Irani, & Ahmad,](#_bookmark21) [2012](#_bookmark21)).

Another important class of porous materials is known as the metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) due to their attractive tuneability, high flexibility, good functionalities and porous structures ([Mahmoud et al.,](#_bookmark43) [2019](#_bookmark43)). These materials have been recently confirmed with excellent advantages in research fields including adsorption and catalysis pro-cesses ([Javanbakht, Pooresmaeil, Hashemi, & Namazi, 2018](#_bookmark19); [Latha,](#_bookmark37) [Devarajan, Karthik, & Suresh, 2020](#_bookmark37); [Liu, Shen, Han, Liu, & Liu, 2019](#_bookmark36); [Salgaonkar, Nadar, & Rathod, 2018](#_bookmark68)). Al-MOFs was synthesized and investigated for aqueous solution treatment from naproxen drug ([Li,](#_bookmark39) [Wang, He, Meng, & Li, 2020](#_bookmark39)). Adsorption and recovery of levofloxacin drug onto iron based MIL-100(Fe) MOFs from aqueous medium was recently explored and reported ([Chaturvedi et al., 2020](#_bookmark26)). The functio-nalization method of poly(4-vinylpyridine) with magnetic copper as an effective and recyclable adsorbent for removal of fluoroquinolone an-tibiotics from aqueous solutions was reported ([Wu, Ma, Li, Guan, &](#_bookmark74) [Chen, 2018](#_bookmark74)). A study was made and reported to investigate MOF-5 by the process of adsorption isotherm, kinetic and thermodynamic para-meters for removal of tetracycline antibiotic from aqueous solutions ([Mirsoleimani-azizi, Setoodeh, & Zeinali, 2018](#_bookmark47)). Synthesis of activated

carbon–HKUST-1-MOFs hybrid material by ultrasonically assisted hy-

drothermal approach and simultaneous ultrasound-assisted removal of antibacterial was investigated by Taguchi optimization ([Azad, Ghaedi,](#_bookmark25) [Dashtian, Hajati, & Pezeshkpour, 2016](#_bookmark25)).

Particularly, tailoring the chemical properties of hydrogels remains a barrier to the successful translation of hydrogels to specific applica-tions, which is important to create high applied performance of func-tional materials. The 3D hydrogel networks can be used to promote the dispersibility of MOFs in hydrogel matrices. Introducing MOFs nano-particles into a hydrogel polymer can cause various positive effects on the chemical structure and significantly change its environmental ap-plications, durability, adsorption capacity as well as mechanical prop-erties. The present study is directed and focused on the assembly of a new nanocomposite based on the potential encapsulation of metal or-ganic frameworks (Zn(GA)) into starch hydrogel matrices and these are doped with magnetic iron oxide (NFe3O4) using microwave irradiation process ([Makhado, Pandey, & Ramontja, 2019](#_bookmark50)) for the formation of a novel NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel. Moreover, metal organic fra-meworks are characterized by high surface area and thus it is expected to exhibit excellent adsorption capacity for removal of different pollu-tants from aqueous solution. On the other hand, hydrogels are also characterized by excellent adsorption capability due to their porous structure. Therefore, combination of these two materials (MOFs and hydrogel) in a new composite will incorporate and afford high surface area as well as porous structure for binding and removing different pollutants. The assembled hydrogel nanosorbent is directed to adsorb fluvastatin drug in presence of different experimental controlling fac-tors and to evaluate the kinetics and adsorption isotherm models as well as thermodynamic parameters.

1. Experimental
    1. _Chemicals and materials_

Iron (III) chloride (FeCl3, 99.9 %), iron (II) chloride (FeCl2, 99.9 %), hydrochloric acid (HCl, 37 %), sodium hydroxide (NaOH, 98.0 %), sodium chloride (NaCl, ≥99.0 %) and starch ((C6H10O5)n, (amylose

17.5 %, amylopectin 82.5 %, MW 692.7 g/mol, moisture content 12.0

%, total ash 0.3 %, assay 99 %) were procured from Sigma Aldrich, USA. Sodium nitrate (NaNO3, 99.9 %), sodium carbonate (Na2CO3, 99.99 %) and sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3, 99 %) were obtained from El-Nasr chemicals, Egypt. Fluvastatin (C24H25FNO4·Na·xH2O, ≥98%, Scheme S1) was obtained from the Nile for Pharmaceuticals Industry, Egypt. Zinc acetate (ZnCH3COOH, 99.99 %), glutaric acid (HOOC(CH2)3COOH, 99 %), malonic acid (CH2(COOH)2, 99 %), sodium sulfate (Na2SO4, 99 %) were purchased from BDH Chemicals, England.

- 1.  _Synthesis_
        1. _Synthesis of starch hydrogel_

Starch powder (2.0 g) was dissolved in 20 mLacetic acid (10 % w/ w) and then added to malonic acid (1.0 g). The mixture was added to 100 mL of deionized water, and stirred vigorously for 3 h, at room temperature. The resulting starch hydrosol was then added dropwise to

1.0 M NaOH solution and stored for 1 h. After filtration, the starch hydrogel were rinsed with an excess of distilled water until a neutral pH value was achieved. The produced starch based hydrogel was dried at 50 °C for 24 h. Scheme S2 demonstrates the possible physical binding (H-bonding) and chemical bond formation between starch and malonic acid cross-linker.

- -   1.  _Synthesis of Zn(GA)-starch hydrogel_

1.0 g of starch hydrogel was dissolved into 100 mL distilled water under room temperature conditions and stirred for 1 h to get homo-geneous solution. Then, the starch solution was dropped into a 100 mL mixture solution containing zinc acetate (0.01 mmol) and glutaric acid (0.01 mmol), and then stirred at room temperature for 30 min followed by heating under microwave irradiation for 3 min. It was washed with ethanol twice and then dried at 50 °C ([Mahmoud, Amira, Seleim, &](#_bookmark46) [Mohamed, 2019](#_bookmark46)). The prepared MOFs-hydrogel (Zn(GA)-Starch hy-drogel) was based on both physical and chemical linkages via H-bonding and ester bond formation between MOFs molecules and polymeric starch matrices.

- -   1.  _Synthesis of magnetic MOFs-starch hydrogel (NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel)_

Synthesis of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (NFe3O4) was ac-complished by the following steps ([Stan et al., 2019a](#_bookmark69), [2019b](#_bookmark70)). A dis-solved mixture of ferric chloride (0.04 mol) and ferrous chloride (0.02 mol) in HCl (0.5 mol L−1) was heated in the microwave for 2 min. Sodium hydroxide (2.0 mol L−1) was then added and heated in the microwave oven for 2 min, washed with distilled water and dried at 60

°C. On the other hand, the preparation of magnetic MOFs-Starch hy-drogel (NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel) was successfully accom-plished by doping nanomagnetic iron oxide into the pores of Zn(GA)-Starch hydrogel by grinding NFe3O4 (1.0 g) with Zn(GA)-Starch hy-drogel (2.0 g) and microwave irradiated for 2.0 min. The prepared NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was based on the physical adsorp-tion chemical binding via elimination of water molecules between doped NFe3O4 and Zn(GA)/starch. Finally, NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was dried at 50 °C for 6 h ([Scheme 1](#_bookmark2)).

- -   1.  _Application of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel for FLV removal from real water matrices_

The eﬃciency of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel for removal of FLV statin drug from real water was examined under optimized ex-perimental conditions (t =30 min, pH = 4 and temperature =25 °C). 10 mL of FLV statin drug (15, 25 and 40 mg L−1) already dissolved in samples of tap water, seawater and industrial wastewater were added to 50 mg of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel, shaking, centrifuging and the values of removal eﬃciency of FLV statin drug from tap water, seawater and industrial wastewater were determined as previously re-ported according to Eq [(1)](#_bookmark3).

- 1.  _Swelling ratio at distinct conditions_

The swelling ratio (SRO) of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was evaluated under different conditions of time, pH and temperature. The impact of time on SRO was evaluated based on keeping the NFe3O4@Zn (GA)/Starch-Hydrogel. After the predetermined time the hydrogel was removed from the deionized water, and the excess of the adsorbed water was removed by filter paper and weighed and the SRO value was

computed from Eq. [2](#_bookmark1). In addition, the impact of pH on SRO was monitored by keeping the hydrogel in deionized water at pH (2–10) for

was monitored according to the following procedure. A mixture con-taining 100 mg of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and 10 mL of FLV statin drug was adjusted at pH 2 and shaken at room temperature. Then, the FLV loaded- NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was rinsed with HCl solution, washed with distilled water and dried at 60 °C ([Mahmoud, El-Said, Rashedy, & Abdelfattah, 2020](#_bookmark45)).

The point-zero charge (pzc) was deduced by mixing 50 mg NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel with 50 mL of KCl (0.01 mol L−1) for tuning the ionic strength of solution. The pH was adjusted to (pH = 2, 3, 4,….12), shaken automatically for 3 h and the finally, the final pH of the mixed solution was measured.

1. Result and discussion
    1. _Characterization of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel_

Fig. S1 represents the FT-IR spectra for the prepared starch hy-drogel, Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel. For starch, the band at 1647 cm−1 is due to adsorbed water in the amorphous regions of starch. The bands between 1400 cm−1 and 1348 cm−1 are assigned to CeOeO stretching and CeOeH bending.

The observed band at 1130 indicates CeO vibration. Bands are also observed at 930 cm−1 (ascribed to CeOeC vibration of α-1,4 glyosidic linkage) and 862 cm−1 (ascribed to CH2 deformation) ([Ngwabebhoh,](#_bookmark54)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)Fig. 1. SEM images of the prepared materials.

[Gazi, & Oladipo, 2016](#_bookmark54)). In addition, Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was characterized by the peaks at 1670, 1400 and 1300 cm−1 that are re-lated to C\]O carboxylic, OH bending as well as CeO stretching, re-spectively ([Luo, Chen, Wu, Yang, & Cheng, 2019](#_bookmark38)). On the other hand, the broad and strong peak at 3400 cm−1 is related to OeH stretching to emphasize the formed intermolecular H-bonding between MOFs and starch hydrogel. Otherwise, the successful doping of iron oxide nano-particles into hydrogel pores was asserted by the peak at 570 cm−1 which is related to Fe-O in NFe3O4 molecules ([Lee, Park, Yoon, & Yang,](#_bookmark40) [2019](#_bookmark40)).

The morphology of starch hydrogel, Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was investigated as demonstrated from the SEM technique. The identified particle size of NFe3O4@Zn (GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was 287.77–291.35 nm. [Fig. 1](#_bookmark4) shows the net-work image of starch hydrogel which is quite different from the desired

Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel ([Fig. 1](#_bookmark4)) in which the binding between MOFs and starch hydrogel for formation of MOFs-based hydrogel as well as the doping NFe3O4 was obviously observed by the change in morphological image of the formed nanocomposite (NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel). On the

The XRD patterns of starch hydrogel, Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel are demonstrated in [Fig. 2](#_bookmark5). The XRD pattern of starch hydrogel has two unique peaks at 2θ = 18° and 30°,

while the XRD of Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel showed new peaks at 2θ =

25, 33, 40 and 45° which are related to the MOFs molecules. The de-fined XRD patterns of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel refer to an amorphous structure ([Fig. 2](#_bookmark5)) ([Mahadevan et al., 2012](#_bookmark49)). On the other hand, Fig. S3 shows the change in XRD pattern NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel after FLV adsorption.

Commonly, the surface area of adsorbent as well as pore size play a significant function in the adsorption and removal processes of ad-sorbate such as drug molecules ([Rajput, Pittman, & Mohan, 2016](#_bookmark60)). Fig. S4 demonstrates the adsorption-desorption surface area of NFe3O4@Zn (GA)/Starch-Hydrogel. The high characterized surface area (528.39 m2/g) of this MOFs-hydrogel nanosorbent assists its removal perfor-mance. The suﬃcient preparation of mesoporous NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel was confirmed by the pore size 2.90 nm which is ca-

tegorized as a mesoporous material (2–50 nm), while the pore volume was found 3.77 cm3/g.

- 1.  _Adsorption experiment for FLV statin drug removal by NFe3O4@Zn (GA)/Starch-Hydrogel_
        1. _pH impact_

The removal of FLV statin drug by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was at most controlled by the influence of solution pHs. As shown in Fig. S5, the removal of FLV statin drug was decreased when the pH increased from 2 to 10 at the different monitored drug con-centrations. The maximum removal eﬃciency of FLV statin drug were 56.25, 63.25 and 72.09% in acidic medium (pH 2), while the minimum removal eﬃciency were 12.25, 19.25 and 28.15% at basic medium (pH 10), Table S3 compiled the absorbance before and after FLV adsorption. On the other hand, the pzc has an important influence on the ad-sorption of FLV statin drug onto NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel (pzc

\= 4). Generally, the surface of investigated nanocomposite was found in different forms according to its pzc, where i) carry a positive charge when pH is lower than its pzc, ii) neutral at pH equal to its pzc and iii) carry a negatively charged surface when pH is higher than its pzc ([Mahmoud, El-Said, Rashedy, & Abdelfattah, 2020](#_bookmark45)). The outlined be-haviors can be used to explain the repulsion occurred between the surface of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel and FLV statin drug (pka

\= 4.56) to inspire the decrease of removal eﬃciency of FLV statin drug as demonstrated in Fig. S5 ([Shah et al., 2018](#_bookmark66)). On the other hand, three types of bonding are expected to take place in this system between FLV and NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel. (i) H-bonding between car-boxylic and OH groups (physisorption), (ii) covalent bond formation between carboxylic and OH groups for the formation of ester group (chemisorption) and (iii) coordinate bond formation between oxygen donor atoms in FLV drug and Zn(II) ion in NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel (chemisorption) as illustrated in Scheme S3.

The R2 values for FLV statin drug removal by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel were 0.9166, 0.9166 and 0.9115 using 15, 20 and 40 mg L−1, respectively to assert that the pore diffusion is a less suitable model to represent this process ([Mahmoud and Mohamed, 2018](#_bookmark42)).

- -   1.  _NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel dose impact_

The dosage of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel is also known as an important parameter to monitor and optimize the adsorption beha-vior for drug removal. As demonstrated in Fig. S6, it can be seen that the augmentation in the removal eﬃciency of FLV statin drug by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel when the dose of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel was increased. The minimum adsorption of FLV statin drug were 11.33, 16.07 and 25.19% using 5 mg for concentration 15, 25 and 40 mg L−1, respectively. On the other hand, the maximum re-movals were 98.24, 89.0 and 84.88% at 100 mg for concentration 15, 25 and 40 mg L−1, respectively. Commonly, the maximum removal of

- -   1.  _FLV statin drug concentration impact and isotherm study_

As shown in [Fig. 4](#_bookmark11)a, the impact of FLV statin drug concentration on the removal by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was investigated under different temperature condition (25, 35 and 45 °C). It was clar-ified that the removal eﬃciency of FLV was increased while the FLV

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The Freundlich isotherm proposes the adsorption of the desired drug molecules on a heterogeneous surface of adsorbent by multilayer formation of the FLV statin drug on the surface of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel. The linear form of Freundlich isotherm was in-vestigated by applying Eq. [(8)](#_bookmark10) and the parameters of this model are compiled in [Table 2](#_bookmark13). The R2 values of FLV statin drug were 0.9681, 0.9665 and 0.9681 at 25, 35 and 45 °C, respectively which confirm that the FLV adsorption onto NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was less favored by the Freundlich isotherm ([Mahmoud, El-Said, Rashedy, &](#_bookmark45) [Abdelfattah, 2020](#_bookmark45)).

log qe = log KF + 1/n log Ce (8)

The Dubinin-Radushkevich (D-R) isotherm equation is more general than the Langmuir model because it does not assume a homogeneous surface or a constant sorption potential or absence of steric hindrance between sorbed and incoming particles. The D-R isotherm equation was used to determine the mean free energy of adsorption. The linear form of this model is represented by following Eq. [(9)](#_bookmark12) ([Zhuang, Kong, Wang,](#_bookmark79) [& Shi, 2019](#_bookmark79)).

ln qe = ln qs − kad ε2 (9)

- -   1.  _Ionic strength impact_

The eﬃciency of FLV statin drug removal by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel was also monitored in presence of distinct electrolytes as chloride, carbonate, nitrate, bicarbonate, phosphate and sulfate so-lutions (0.1 mol L−1). The presence of electrolyte caused a slight de-crease in the removal eﬃciency of FLV statin drug by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/ Starch-Hydrogel as demonstrated in Fig. S7. The adsorption eﬃciency decreased from 65.14 % to 62.05, 50.74, 62.65, 60.07, 63.18 and 48.79

% in the presence of chloride, carbonate, nitrate, bicarbonate, phos-phate and sulfate, respectively for concentration 15 mg L−1 of FLV statin drug. The same behavior was recognized for the other evaluated FLV statin drug concentrations (25 and 40 mg L−1) as illustrated (Fig. S7). The recognized adsorption values obtained from this study con-cluded that the NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel is an eﬃcient ad-sorbent for FLV statin drug removal in the presence of different elec-trolyte solutions ([Wang et al., 2018](#_bookmark75)).

The removal processes of pharmaceuticals are mainly affected by adsorbent properties (i.e., surface area, pore size distribution, and surface functional groups), characteristic properties of adsorbate (pka) as well as experimental conditions (pH, time, mass, concentration, temperature). The concluded removal capacities of FLV statin drug onto NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel (782.05 mg g−1), Zn(GA) (534.09 mg g−1) and Starch-Hydrogel (212.67 mg g−1) at optimum conditions (pH = 4, time =30 min, concentration = 40 mg L−1, temperature 25

The removal of FLV statin drug from different water samples by the action of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was examined at the se-lected optimum conditions as compiled in Table S5. The percentage values of FLV statin drug removal from tap water were 98.74, 98.91 and

_pseudo_ \-second _pseudo_ \-second _pseudo_ \-second _pseudo_ \-second _pseudo_ \-second

The swelling ratio (SRO) is a remarkable factor used to monitor the capacity of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel to absorb water. Additionally, the SRO has a significant effect on the adsorption eﬃ-ciency of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel for FLV statin drug re-moval ([Fosso-Kankeu, Cilliers, & Pandey, 2019](#_bookmark33)). [Fig. 6](#_bookmark16) represents the swelling ratio at different conditions, viz., time, pH and temperature. The increase in time has mainly caused an obvious increase in the SRO ([Fig. 6](#_bookmark16)a) due to the positive effect on the swelling of internal pores of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel as well as surface swelling. More-over, the SRO of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was increased from 500 to 1000% when the solution pH was increased from increasing the pH value from 2 to 10. Generally, at low pH, the high hydrogen ions caused an increasing behavior in the physical cross-linking to lead to shrinking of hydrogel (decrease swelling). On the other hand, at high pH, the high hydroxyl groups in solution were forced to repulse with the hydroxyl groups on the hydroxyl surface to cause noticeable in-crease in the SRO ([Sadasivuni et al., 2016](#_bookmark65)). Finally, the SRO was found to increase from 500 to 800% when the temperature increased from 25 to 80 °C ([Fig. 6](#_bookmark16)c). This behavior may be related to the disturbance in the H-bonding between the polymeric hydrogel networks due to increasing in the temperature and thus enhancing the SRO ([Rao, Kumar, & Han,](#_bookmark62) [2017](#_bookmark62)).

The recycling of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel is a remarkable factor to investigate the economical application of this nanocomposite in FLV statin drug removal from aqueous solution. The loaded FLV onto NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was rinsed with a regenerating re-agent as HCl (0.1 mol L−1) ([Liao & Huang, 2019](#_bookmark23)) and the adsorption capacity of the recycled NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was suc-cessively examined for five cycles. Fig. S8 illustrates that the removal capacity of FLV statin by NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was

Adsorbent

slightly decreased from 782.45 to 700.09 mg g−1 after five regenera-tion cycles to confirm the validity of multi-step applications of NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel.

1. Conclusion

A magnetic MOFs-Starch hydrogel was designed and synthesized based on cross-linking of starch hydrogel with MOFs, while the mag-netic iron oxide nanoparticles were doped into the MOFs-based hy-drogel matrix. The maximum swelling ratio 1000.0% was established at pH 10, 180 min and 25 °C. The assembled NFe3O4@Zn(GA)/Starch-Hydrogel was optimized to evaluate removal of FLV statin drug from

aqueous solution. The adsorption of FLV statin drug by NFe O @Zn
